claim_text: As part of Microsoft’s commitment to disclose information about our environmental footprint, the following sections are a compilation of environmental metrics across greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, energy, water, waste and circularity, and land.
source_excerpt: As part of Microsoft’s commitment to disclose information about our environmental footprint, the following sections are a compilation of environmental metrics across greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, energy, water, waste and circularity, and land.

claim_text: Microsoft's Scope 1 and 2 (market-based) emissions for FY24 are 402,600 metric tons of CO2e.
Microsoft's Scope 3 emissions for FY24 are 15,140,000 metric tons of CO2e.
Microsoft's total emissions (Scope 1 + 2 + 3) for FY24 are 15,543,000 metric tons of CO2e.
Microsoft defines carbon neutrality as matching the emissions within the carbon neutrality boundary with an equivalent amount of carbon credits.
source_excerpt: Microsoft defines carbon neutrality as matching the emissions within the carbon neutrality boundary with an equivalent amount of carbon credits as shown in this table.

claim_text: Microsoft has maintained carbon neutrality every year since FY13.
source_excerpt: This data supports Microsoft’s target to be carbon neutral every year since FY13.

claim_text: Microsoft has maintained its commitment to carbon neutrality while progressing towards a carbon negative goal.
source_excerpt: As we have made progress towards our carbon negative commitment, which includes purchasing carbon removal credits, we have also maintained carbon neutrality.

claim_text: Microsoft only applies carbon removal credits against its carbon neutral boundary if they have been retired and delivered.

claim_text: Microsoft has identified partnerships through two leading land protection organizations, the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation (NFWF) within the United States and The Nature Conservancy (TNC) globally.
source_excerpt: Since announcing this commitment in April 2020, Microsoft has identified partnerships through two leading land protection organizations, the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation (NFWF) within the United States and The Nature Conservancy (TNC) globally, to partner with on our land protection journey.

claim_text: Microsoft aims to be carbon negative by 2030 and remove from the atmosphere an equivalent amount of all the carbon dioxide our company has emitted either directly or by our electricity consumption since we were founded in 1975.
source_excerpt: Microsoft announced in January 2020 that we aim to be carbon negative by 2030 and that by 2050 we aim to remove from the atmosphere an equivalent amount of all the carbon dioxide our company has emitted either directly or by our electricity consumption since we were founded in 1975.

claim_text: We plan to achieve this commitment by reducing our Scope 1 and 2 (market-based) emissions to near zero by increasing energy efficiency, decarbonizing our operations, and reaching 100% direct renewable electricity by 2025.
source_excerpt: We plan to achieve this commitment by reducing our Scope 1 and 2 (market-based) emissions to near zero by increasing energy efficiency, decarbonizing our operations, and reaching 100% direct renewable electricity by 2025.

claim_text: Microsoft’s GHG inventory includes five of the seven GHGs addressed by the Kyoto Protocol—carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N O), hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), and sulfur hexafluoride (SF6).
source_excerpt: Microsoft’s GHG inventory includes five of the seven GHGs addressed by the Kyoto Protocol—carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N O), hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), and sulfur hexafluoride (SF6).

claim_text: This carbon inventory reflects what is in scope for our carbon negative commitment.
source_excerpt: This carbon inventory reflects what is in scope for our carbon negative commitment.

claim_text: Microsoft uses an operational control approach for setting organizational boundaries and for corporate reporting of GHG emissions, energy, water, waste and circularity, and ecosystem metrics.

claim_text: We have published the criteria we use to help ensure that the carbon removal credits that we contract are high quality: Microsoft Criteria for High-Quality Carbon Dioxide Removal.
source_excerpt: We have published the criteria we use to help ensure that the carbon removal credits that we contract are high quality: Microsoft Criteria for High-Quality Carbon Dioxide Removal.

claim_text: Microsoft procures renewable energy from on-site generation, unbundled EACs, PPAs, and green power products.
source_excerpt: Microsoft procures renewable energy from on-site generation, unbundled EACs, PPAs, and green power products.

claim_text: Purchased EACs include renewable energy certificates (RECs) (Green-e certified), guarantees of origin (GOs), renewable energy GOs (REGOs), International RECs (I-RECs), Tradable Instruments for Global Renewables (TIGRs), New Zealand Energy Certificate System (NZECS) certificates, J-Credits, Non-Fossil Fuel Certificates (NFCs), large-scale generation certificates (LGC), Green Electricity Certificates (GECs), Taiwan Renewable Energy Certificates (T-RECs), and PowerPlus.
source_excerpt: Purchased EACs include renewable energy certificates (RECs) (Green-e certified), guarantees of origin (GOs), renewable energy GOs (REGOs), International RECs (I-RECs), Tradable Instruments for Global Renewables (TIGRs), New Zealand Energy Certificate System (NZECS) certificates, J-Credits, Non-Fossil Fuel Certificates (NFCs), large-scale generation certificates (LGC), Green Electricity Certificates (GECs), Taiwan Renewable Energy Certificates (T-RECs), and PowerPlus.

claim_text: To calculate Scope 2 emissions from a market-based approach, Microsoft captures the impact across all renewable electricity purchases and matches that with the markets where we operate.

source_excerpt: Microsoft’s water inventory includes withdrawal, consumption, and discharge volumes associated with assets under our operational control.

claim_text: We include operational waste, product packaging recyclability, and single-use plastics in our waste and circularity metrics.
source_excerpt: We include operational waste, product packaging recyclability, and single-use plastics in our waste and circularity metrics.

claim_text: For product packaging, both recyclability and single-use plastics metrics cover all Microsoft hardware packaging (retail and commercial) and consumer software packaging of the products available to be sold during the reporting year.
source_excerpt: For product packaging, both recyclability and single-use plastics metrics cover all Microsoft hardware packaging (retail and commercial) and consumer software packaging of the products available to be sold during the reporting year.

claim_text: Similarly, these metrics support our product packaging targets: to make fully recyclable product packaging by 2030 and to eliminate single-use plastics in product packaging by the end of 2025.
source_excerpt: Similarly, these metrics support our product packaging targets: to make fully recyclable product packaging by 2030 and to eliminate single-use plastics in product packaging by the end of 2025.

claim_text: Microsoft calculates and reports Scope 3 emissions for all relevant categories.

claim_text: We use primary data to calculate emissions for both Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions. Where primary data is not available, we use estimates.

claim_text: Microsoft uses the 100-year Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Fourth Assessment Report for global warming potential values.
source_excerpt: Microsoft uses the 100-year Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Fourth Assessment Report for global warming potential values.

claim_text: In FY23, Microsoft started using LCAs to calculate the emissions associated with the manufacture of devices that we sold during the reporting year.
